drafted_from: tool:see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens row in tool-rows.json, do-work/see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens.mjs, src/pursuit-lens.mjs, read-data/see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens.json and test/see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens.test.mjs; list:pursuit-lens fields read with records:read
start_here: Say to your AI: "Tell me how to look at what I am pursuing through my pursuit lens, the short paragraph and the full setup with every part and its rows." It runs tool:see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens, reads your lens rows and answers the paragraph every AI reads when it connects and the setup.

lists.label: Pursuit lens
lists.holds: The rows of your lens: for each part of what you pursue, what to look for and what to ask or do; the parts and the opening and closing words are kept in your content settings.

values.ask_or_do: ask which bed they would save first
name the date of the last frost

instructions: 1. Pour the example lens rows into the list you keep interview or discovery prompts in (see pour), or make list:pursuit-lens from them; keep the lens's opening, parts and closing in your content settings row, or hand the whole lens in.

2. Say "How should an AI look at what I pursue?"; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens, with answer paragraph, setup or both (the default) and optionally lens {opening, parts, closing, rows}.

3. Read the answer: paragraph is the opening, each part in one sentence and the closing; setup holds every part with each row's look_for and ask_or_do, the joining interview rows (those marked joining_interview) and where its answers are kept; joining_interview_file names that file.
4. It writes nothing; with no lens in your lists and none handed in it says what to hand in or keep first.

worked_examples.title: A gardener's lens handed in, paragraph only
worked_examples.ask: Give me the paragraph an AI should read to look at what a gardener pursues.

lens.opening: Look at what the gardener tends.
lens.closing: Then pick one bed to work.

rows.ask_or_do: ask which bed they would save first
name the date of the last frost

worked_examples.given: From tools/see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens/test/see-a-pursuit-through-the-lens.test.mjs: the made-up gardener lens above, handed in. With answer "both" the same lens also answers the setup.
worked_examples.hands_back: {paragraph: "Look at what the gardener tends. Soil: what feeds the plant Weather: what comes from outside Then pick one bed to work.", joining_interview_file: "/Pursuits/joining interview.json"} (no setup key for answer paragraph). With answer setup the setup holds how "Look at what the gardener tends.", parts Soil and Weather with one row each, joining_interview.rows [{look_for: "what they water every day", ask_or_do: "ask which bed they would save first"}] and then "Then pick one bed to work.".

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
